name: Český Krumlov
title: Holidays in Český Krumlov
intro: A fairytale Czech town wrapped in a loop of river, with a painted castle tower, cobbled lanes and rafting through the middle. Here's what Český Krumlov is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Český Krumlov lit up at dusk inside a loop of the Vltava river
facts_note: The Czech Republic is in the Schengen area, so the new EU entry checks apply. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May to September is best, warm for walking and rafting the Vltava. The Five-Petalled Rose Festival brings medieval costumes in June. December has a small Christmas market and the town looks magical in snow. Day-trippers fill the town at midday, so stay a night.

things.name: Český Krumlov Castle
things.blurb: A huge castle with a painted tower, gardens and a rare baroque theatre.

things.name: Castle tower
things.blurb: Climb the tower for the view over the river loop and rooftops.

things.name: Rafting on the Vltava
things.blurb: Paddle a raft or canoe through the town, easy enough for families.

things.name: Old town
things.blurb: A UNESCO-listed maze of lanes, little squares and pubs.

things.name: Egon Schiele Art Centre
things.blurb: Works by the Austrian artist who lived here.

things.name: Seminary Garden
things.blurb: A viewpoint over the castle and river.

faqs.question: Is Český Krumlov worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the most beautiful small towns in Europe. It gets busy at midday, so stay overnight.

faqs.question: How do you get to Český Krumlov?
faqs.answer: Fly into Prague, then take a bus or shuttle, about 3 hours. Linz in Austria is about 1 hour 15 minutes away.

faqs.question: Can you do Český Krumlov as a day trip from Prague?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it's a long day. Staying a night is much better.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Český Krumlov?
How many days do you need in Český Krumlov?
faqs.answer: One or two days covers the castle, town and a river trip.
